statement: For independent Bernoulli bond percolation on the infinite d-regular tree T_d, d >= 3, p_c = 1/(d-1) and p_u = 1.
assumptions: Infinite connected d-regular tree
Integer d >= 3
Independent undirected edges, each open with probability p
p_u is the infimum of parameters with almost-surely exactly one infinite cluster

source.prior_art: Classical regular-tree boundary; no novelty claim

proof: Away from the root, the open descendants are a Galton-Watson process with Binomial(d-1,p) offspring. Its survival probability is positive exactly when (d-1)p>1, and is zero at criticality since d>=3 and the offspring law is nondegenerate. This gives p_c. For p_c<p<1 fix an infinite deterministic ray and choose a hanging subtree off each ray vertex. The events that the edge attaching that subtree is closed and that its root has an infinite open descendant cluster are independent across these pairwise edge-disjoint subtrees, each with probability (1-p) times the positive survival probability. Almost surely infinitely many occur. They create distinct infinite clusters because a tree has no alternate route around the closed attaching edge. Thus uniqueness fails for every p<1 (below and at p_c there are no infinite clusters), while at p=1 the entire connected tree is the single infinite cluster.
remaining_gap: No gap in this special-case proof claimed; independent audit pending. Extension to arbitrary nonamenable Cayley graphs remains open in this packet.

statement: Let G_N=Cay(F_2,{a^k:1<=|k|<=N} union {b,b^-1}), N>=1. For independent bond percolation, p_c(G_N) is the unique alpha_N in (0,1) satisfying alpha_N(2chi_N(alpha_N)-1)=1, where chi_N(p) is the expected root-cluster size on Z with edges of lengths 1,...,N. There is no infinite cluster at alpha_N, and p_u(G_N)=1.
assumptions: F_2 freely generated by a and b
Finite integer N>=1
Undirected simple graph with the stated symmetric generating set
Independent identically distributed bond states
chi_N is for bond percolation on the factor graph, not the full Cayley graph
proof: Disjoint closed cuts give finite horizontal clusters and continuous chi_N for p<1. Contracting a-lines in the ordinary free-group tree leaves a tree of lines, with every b-edge a bridge. After arrival through one b-edge, a fresh horizontal cluster of size K has 2K-1 unexposed b-edges to distinct new lines. Independent factor and bridge states give exact iid offspring Binomial(2K-1,p), with mean p(2chi_N-1). Galton-Watson extinction and survival give the unique critical equation. Its offspring is nondegenerate, so critical extinction holds. For p>alpha_N, independently isolating infinitely many pairwise disjoint hanging components by closed b-bridges produces infinitely many infinite clusters; at p=1 there is one. Full proof in ATTEMPT.md.
remaining_gap: Special-case independence and topology require audit. The general Cayley graph lacks the factor-tree decomposition; no extension is proved.
novelty: Published free-product specialization; not claimed new

statement: For G_N in L1, degree D=2N+2, edge-isoperimetric infimum phi_E=2, normalized conductance h=1/(N+1), and N/(N+1)<=rho<=(N-1+sqrt(3))/(N+1)<1 for uniform simple random walk. Thus on the fixed group F_2, rho tends to 1 along simple generating sets although each graph has p_c<p_u=1; no positive spectral gap uniform over all its generating sets exists.
assumptions: All assumptions of L1
rho is the l2 norm of the uniform simple-random-walk operator
phi_E counts unoriented edges with exactly one endpoint in A
Normalized conductance is phi_E/D

source.prior_art: Juschenko-Nagnibeda arXiv:1206.2183v3 Section 1 already discusses adding powers to make rho approach one

proof: The spanning 4-regular tree gives boundary at least 2|A| for every finite A. A_L={a^j:0<=j<L}, L>=N, has boundary 2L+N(N+1), proving phi_E=2. Its indicator has Rayleigh quotient N/(N+1)-N/(2L), giving the lower rho bound in the limit. Split adjacency into the ordinary-tree operator of norm 2sqrt(3) and 2N-2 unitary translations, proving the upper bound by the triangle inequality. ATTEMPT.md supplies the parent-child quadratic-form proof of the tree norm bound.
remaining_gap: Audit pending; this refutes a uniform spectral-gap bridge only and does not refute C0047.

statement: The cited normalized spectral sufficient condition is D*rho*p_c<1, where D is graph degree and rho is normalized simple-random-walk spectral radius. The existing C0047-A001 route's repeated p_c<1/rho omits D. The degree-free inequality is automatic for rho<1 and p_c<=1 and supplies no proof of p_c<p_u.
assumptions: Connected regular Cayley graph of finite degree D
Independent Bernoulli bond percolation
rho is normalized simple-random-walk spectral radius
This corrects a source criterion, not the statement of the parent conjecture

statement: The stronger auxiliary claim that D*rho*p_c<1 holds for every nonamenable simple Cayley graph is false. On the standard 4-regular Cayley tree of F_2, p_c=1/3, p_u=1, rho=sqrt(3)/2, and D*rho*p_c=2sqrt(3)/3>1. Therefore the published sufficient condition is not necessary for p_c<p_u.
assumptions: Standard symmetric generating set {a,a^-1,b,b^-1} of F_2
Independent bond percolation
Uniform normalized simple random walk

source.location: ATTEMPT.md: concrete correction and radial test functions
source.support: L0 plus explicit tree spectral proof; published criterion in C0

counterexample: L0 proves p_c=1/3 and p_u=1. Orienting toward an end bounds the tree adjacency norm above by 2sqrt(3). Truncated radial functions f_R(v)=3^(-dist(e,v)/2) have squared norm 1+4R/3 and adjacency quadratic form 8R/sqrt(3), attaining that upper bound in the limit. Dividing by D=4 gives rho=sqrt(3)/2, and the product equals 2sqrt(3)/3>1.
remaining_gap: Independent review pending. The parent conjecture is satisfied in this counterexample, so it is not refuted.

statement: For G_N in L1, 1/(2N+1)<=p_c(G_N)<1/3 for N>=2, p_c<= (sqrt(1+16N)-1)/(8N), and for every N>=2 p_c is at most the unique r in (0,1/3) with 4r^4-8r^3+7r^2+2r-1=0.
assumptions: All assumptions of L1
Quartic root is an upper bound and is not asserted equal to p_c
proof: The degree-based self-avoiding-path union bound gives the lower bound. Counting directly open neighbors gives chi_N>=1+2Np; substitute in the exact offspring mean. Under the monotone nearest-neighbor/long-edge coupling, events of a root length-two edge open and the corresponding nearest edge closed add the distinct vertices +2 and -2, each with probability p(1-p). Hence chi_N>=chi_1+2p(1-p). Substitution in p(2chi_N-1) gives the quartic upper bound and strictly lowers the root from 1/3. The pointwise indicators add; no independence between these two gain events is needed.
remaining_gap: The bounded arithmetic checks passed (128 configurations, five boundary/Rayleigh cases); independent mathematical review remains pending. No exact numeric alpha_N for N>=2 is claimed.
